subdomain: 3.5 Design a RAG pipeline with appropriate chunking and indexing strategies

en.question: For compound repair procedures, small fixed chunks retrieve exact steps but omit prerequisites in adjacent sections. Whole-document chunks retain prerequisites but fill the generation budget with unrelated procedures. The team must choose a chunking and indexing strategy without increasing that budget. Which experiment provides the most relevant evidence?

options.text: Keep whole-document chunks and compare only which embedding model gives the highest similarity score.
options.note: Raw similarity scores do not establish that the final context contains complete procedures within budget. This comparison leaves the demonstrated granularity problem unchanged.

options.text: Adopt the chunk size used in a published vendor benchmark and skip corpus-specific validation.
options.note: Published settings describe a particular corpus and evaluation. They do not establish the right boundaries or overlap for these cross-section repair dependencies.

options.text: Keep the smallest chunks and maximize top-K until every neighboring section enters generation.
options.note: Increasing top-K can consume the fixed generation budget and add distracting material. It does not test whether better boundaries can preserve dependencies more selectively.

options.text: Rebuild candidate indexes with procedure-aware boundaries and tested overlap, then compare dependency coverage and final-answer quality at the fixed budget.
options.note: Boundary and overlap changes must be reflected in the indexed chunks before retrieval can be evaluated. Testing complete evidence and final outcomes identifies a workable balance between fragmented and overlarge chunks.

references.title: Anthropic: Define success criteria and build evaluations
